chapter: First bands, illness and Houston life
title: First summer tour with Frank Davis and the Harlem Grill with Chester Boone
summary: At sixteen Cobb tours Louisiana with Frank Davis, then joins Chester Boone's band at the Harlem Grill for $34 a week while his mother earned $10; the dates are sorted out along the way.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, that makes you 18.
Pardon?
That makes you 18 years old?
No, I'm not 18 yet, now.
Now wait a minute. '36 . . . You were born in '18, he was
Now you've got to get your calculus together.
Yeah, I know.
No, you've right. If you were born in 1918...
Okay. I was born in 1918. I joined Milton in '36.
1936 is 18 years later.
Wait just a second. What did you do in between the time you were with this stage band and Larkin? Milt Loggins? Or did you go from the stage band to Milt?
No, no.
Oh, I thought ...
Let me tell you what happened. My first summer month that I went out professionally, I went out with

a guy from Louisiana by the name of Frank Davis, and this was in 1934 during the summer month when school was out. And, of course, I was the youngest guy in the group, at my age, and I have to think what age I was then, because you're turning me down; you can figure it by years if I was born in '18, and school month come out before August come in, and my birthday is August 10th, and of course, anywhere I went they'd have to come and consult my mother and be responsible for me as the leader.
That's the way it was. And if you didn't do that, I couldn't go, see? During those days, parents were strict, and mine were very strict.

Now, we went out like 3 months all over the state of Louisiana, because he is from Louisiana. I come back here and I go back to school in September. Now, on that band was a guy by the name of Chester Boone that liked my playing, and he had formed a band in Houston, and went into the Harlem Grill here in Houston, Texas.
You said Chuck Boone?
No, I said Chester. C-h-e-s-t-e-r, Chester Boone
Oh, Chester Boone. He was a saxophone player, wasn't he?
He was a trumpet player.
Well, there was a Chester Boone...
Chester Boone
But wasn't there a Chester Boone that was a saxophone player? (Lester Boone - ed.)
I don't know.
From Chicago?
I don't know, but I come back the same year, in '34, and he formed a band to go in to the Harlem Grill here in Houston on West Dallas for 6 nights a week. (unintelligible)
Wow.

Now my mother is working, making $10 a week, and I'm getting $34 a week for 6 nights a week. But the ironic situation was I went to worked at rehearsal for the job and went home to do my studies for school, and take me a nap and go to work and missed the first night! I knew I lost my job, but I didn't.

I woke up in 2 o'clock in the morning, and Helen, you didn't hear me, did you? everything was finis then. Well, I'm telling the truth. But I was all right after that. And I stayed with Chester for 2 years -- from '34 to '36, and that's when I transferred and went over ... (end TAPE SIDE 1)
